declared.title: A Mixed-Methods Cluster Randomised Waitlist-Controlled Trial of a Goal-Based Behaviour Change Intervention Implemented in Workplaces
declared.venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 11); OpenAlex search « Kudrna mental contrasting implementation intentions workplace cluster randomised trial » (2026-11-26)

population: 225 staff of 28 UK workplaces; all wrote down health and wellbeing wishes, the intervention arm added obstacles and if-then plans (MCII)

findings.text: Adding obstacles and if-then plans (MCII) to thinking about one's wishes did not improve self-reported progress four weeks later

support.sentence: The results showed no substantive effect of the intervention on average self-reported progress towards what they wished to do for their health and wellbeing four weeks later (mean difference on a 1-7 scale: -0.19; 95% credible interval: -1.08-0.71).

findings.text: Unexpectedly, anxiety rose in the MCII arm, and men and people of Asian ethnicity may have progressed less

support.sentence: Unexpectedly, anxiety increased, and we found evidence that might suggest people identifying as men or of Asian ethnicity made less progress in the intervention group.

limits: small cluster trial (28 workplaces); progress self-reported on a 1-7 scale four weeks later
the control arm only wrote down wishes: the closest test of MCII against only wishing
independent of the creators of MCII; workplace goals often blocked by outside barriers (focus groups)
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
